text: #814: a lock pins each statement's layout as well as its text. A pin hashes a statement's canonical text, which collapses whitespace, and TLA+ reads a bulleted list of /\ or \/ by its columns, so re-indenting a ratified statement could change what TLC checks and keep its pin. Beside each statement's pin, a lock records a layout pin: the SHA-256 of the definitions the pin covers as written, with comments blanked in place, the space at each line's end trimmed and blank lines dropped, so every token keeps its line and column; editing or adding a comment changes no layout pin, and moving a token does. New ratifications hash both pins, so the layout a person saw is the layout that's pinned. A lock ratified before this keeps its pins and proposal hash, so its ratifying comment or decision still checks; it gains its layout pins once, by migration, from the model at the commit that recorded its ratification, the one that wrote its proposal into the lock, as migrated layout pins its proposal leaves out. CI refuses a layout pin's change without a new ratification: a ratified layout pin is in the proposal, and the ratification check holds a migrated one to the model at every commit that recorded the lock's proposal, on any branch the history holds, and refuses a lock whose migrated layout pins were removed. The gate checks both pins and reports a layout mismatch as its own failure, naming the definition and the first line that moved when it can read the model as ratified. A lock without layout pins, as in a repository that hasn't migrated, keeps verifying: its pins are checked as before, and its receipt says its layout isn't pinned yet.
